reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E3 shows oxide films reduce wear in HEAs but does not address nanocrystalline structure, strain accommodation, or a pre-formed scale. E5 shows heat treatment affects wear but at room temperature and without characterizing an oxide scale. E1 and E4 discuss microstructural refinement and deformation but are unrelated to oxide scale formation or high-temperature wear. E2 describes dynamic amorphization, a competing mechanism, and is listed as conflicting. The premises are largely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: A pre-formed nanocrystalline oxide scale on FeNiCrCoCu can act as a passivating barrier that limits further oxidation and reduces metal-to-metal contact.
The nanocrystalline structure of the oxide scale allows it to deform and accommodate strain without cracking under cyclic loading.
Pre-wear annealing at 600°C in controlled atmosphere produces a coherent, well-adhered, nanocrystalline oxide scale on the coating.
This oxide scale reduces adhesive wear, abrasive wear, and spallation at high temperatures (500–700°C).
The resulting tribological improvement is measurable as lower friction coefficient and reduced wear rate compared to an as-deposited coating.
